research_result.description: The Threads API allows developers to programmatically publish text, image, video, and carousel posts, manage replies, search locations, retrieve media, and access account and post insights.
research_result.credential_requirements: Developers must create a Meta App with the Threads Use Case to obtain a Threads App ID and Threads App Secret. Access tokens conform to OAuth 2.0 and are generated via an Authorization Window flow. Short-lived user access tokens can be exchanged server-side for long-lived tokens (valid for 60 days). Development and testing with designated Threads Testers is free, but access for general production users requires passing Meta's App Review process.

evidence.claim: Threads API authentication uses user access tokens conforming to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

evidence.claim: General production access for app users without an explicit app role requires Meta App Review approval.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: In order for app users without a role on your app to be able to grant your app these permissions, each permission must first be approved through the App Review process, and your app must be published.

evidence.claim: The Threads API is accessible via graph.threads.com or graph.threads.net REST endpoints.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The Threads API can be accessed by either `graph.threads.com` or `graph.threads.net`.

evidence.claim: The Threads API is self-serve and accessible to all developers.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Today at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, we announced that the Threads API is now available to all developers.

evidence.claim: MCP servers are available for integrating AI agents with the Threads API.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Unofficial MCP server for Meta's Threads API. Enables LLMs like Claude to publish posts, manage replies, and track insights through the Model Context Protocol.
